newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish right, ex-communists running level in polls.
newsitem.headline: Polish right, ex-communists running level in polls.

text.p: Poland's co-ruling ex-communist party and the newly formed rightist opposition bloc led by the Solidarity trade union are running neck-in-neck in public opinion polls ahead of this year's parliamentary elections.

A survey by the private Demoskop agency, released on Thursday, showed the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) was backed by 23 percent of voters while Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) had 22 percent.
The poll indicated the SLD's popularity had remained flat since December while the Solidarity bloc's had risen by a point.
An earlier poll by public television's OBOP agency, showed Solidarity with 29 percent support while the ex-communists, in power since 1993, had only 25 percent.
Analysts say that either of the two groups could form a coalition government after the elections, scheduled after August this year, with smaller parties holding a balance of power.

The Demoskop poll showed the co-ruling Polish Peasant Party (PSL) would end up as the third strongest party in parliament if elections were held now. The PSL is keeping its options open about a future coalition partnership.
The most market reform-oriented party, the centrist Union for Freedom, placed fourth in the Demoskop poll with 12 percent support.

The survey, with a 3.2 percent error margin, showed two more parties would pass the five percent threshold needed to enter parliament -- the radical right Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) and the leftist Union of Labour (ROP).
